In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of factors that regulate the F plasmids of Escherichiacoli and other Gram-negative bacteria.
how the F plasmids respond to the Cpx stress pathway and how this response is controlled.
the identification of the mechanism of downregulation of the positive regulator, TraJ, in response to the activation of the CxP stress response in Escherichia Coli.

the F plasmids have a mechanism to sense and respond to the Cpx stress envelope stress response.
the Cpx stress system is a negative regulator of F transfer, which is activated in response to envelope stress.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cpx stress pathway is involved in the downregulation and instability of TraJ, and that this is mediated by a posttranslational mechanism.

the Cpx stress system is a regulator of F plasmid replication.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CpxA* gain of function does not result in a constitutive activation of the CxP stress response, but rather a hyperactivation of the Cpx response in the presence of a stress signal.
the F plasmids are not the only plasmids that are affected by the Cpx stress pathway, as TraJ is also downregulated in the presence of the cpxA gain-of-function mutations.
the F tra operon is regulated in response to the Cpx stress envelope response, which is induced by a variety of stress conditions, such as misfolding of proteins in the peripalasm.
